handbookNote: New Jersey Commercial Driver's License Manual (base AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' content, cover Version: March 2025, most sections Version: July 2017, Section 11 Vehicle Inspection modernized to Version: March 2025), published by the New Jersey Motor Vehicle Commission (MVC) -- fetched directly from https://www.nj.gov/mvc/pdf/license/CDL_Manual.pdf on 2026-08-23 (7.8MB PDF, full text extracted via pdftotext -layout to scratchpad/nj_cdl_research/nj_cdl_manual_full.txt, 9,594 lines, cross-checked against a pdftotext -raw extraction (nj_cdl_manual_raw.txt) for two-column sections). Price matches this project's established CDL tier ($6.99). Exam mechanics: unlike many other states built in this project, New Jersey's own official MVC website (not just the manual) explicitly discloses CDL knowledge-test mechanics -- the official page https://www.nj.gov/mvc/drivertopics/cdltest.htm (fetched 2026-08-23) states verbatim: 'The knowledge test is a 50-question general test with additional separate tests for each endorsement. To pass the test you must answer at least 80% of the questions correctly.' This is a CONFIRMED official figure (50 questions / 80% passing on the General Knowledge test), not a third-party estimate -- consistent with the federally standardized minimum passing score of 80 percent (49 CFR 383.135(a)). The per-item counts for the individual endorsement knowledge tests (air brakes, combination, doubles/triples, hazmat, passenger, school bus, tank) are NOT disclosed by the official source and are left hedged/unconfirmed in this track's exam-mechanics copy; third-party CDL test-prep sites were not relied on for this gap since the official mechanics page already provided the material fact for the primary General Knowledge test. Other officially confirmed NJ CDL process details from the same MVC page: the knowledge test fee is $125; you must obtain an Examination Test Receipt (with 6 Points of ID) before testing; test scores are valid for 360 days; you must practice at least 14 days accompanied by a licensed CDL holder before the road (skills) test; if you fail the knowledge test you must wait 7 days before retaking it, may retake as many times as needed, but must renew the Test Receipt if not passed within 180 days; effective 2/7/22, HAZMAT-endorsement applicants must complete Entry Level Driver Training (ELDT) from an FMCSA Training Provider Registry (TPR) provider before taking the knowledge test, and ELDT completion is required before the skills test for a first-time CDL or any endorsement; the CDL Skills Test (road test) has three graded parts (pre-trip inspection, basic control skills, road skills), requires an appointment, and failing it requires at least a 2-week wait to retake (up to 6 months after repeated failures); CDL skills test scores may be 'banked' per a specific set of MVC rules (pre-trip portion must be passed first, site-specific, valid for one CLP cycle of 180 days). Content-depth rationale: New Jersey uses the same AAMVA-authored Modernized Testing System base manual as several other recently built CDL-track states in this project (e.g. Kentucky, Louisiana, Massachusetts, Missouri, Nebraska), organized into the same 13 core sections, and notably contains NO New Jersey-specific front-matter insert (the fetched manual text contains zero occurrences of the word 'Jersey' -- it is the pure AAMVA base manual as adopted, unlike some other states' manuals which layer in state-specific administrative sections). Sections: Section 1 Introduction (CDL classes A/B/C, six endorsements T/N/H/X/S/P, ten restriction codes, disqualifications, medical/self-certification, International Registration Plan/IFTA) mapped to bucket 01_licensing; Section 2 Driving Safely (the largest section, split into two buckets: 02_driving_safely_a covering vehicle inspection, basic control, shifting, communicating, controlling speed, managing space, seeing hazards, distracted driving, aggressive drivers, night/fog/winter/hot-weather driving, railroad crossings, and mountain driving; 03_driving_safely_b covering driving emergencies, antilock braking systems, skid control/recovery, accident procedures, fires, alcohol/drugs, and hazardous materials rules for all commercial drivers); Section 3 Transporting Cargo Safely mapped to 04_cargo; Section 4 Transporting Passengers Safely mapped to 05_passenger; Section 5 Air Brakes mapped to 06_air_brakes; Section 6 Combination Vehicles mapped to 07_combination; Section 7 Doubles and Triples mapped to 08_doubles_triples; Section 8 Tank Vehicles mapped to 09_tank; Section 9 Hazardous Materials split into three buckets (10_hazmat_a covering 9.1-9.3: intent of the regulations, shipper/carrier/driver responsibilities, and communication rules/placarding; 10c_hazmat_loading covering 9.4-9.5.2: loading/unloading requirements, precautions for specific hazard classes, the Do Not Load table, bulk-packaging markings, and cargo-tank attendance rules -- added as a targeted gap-fill bucket after a self-review found this subsection's line range had been skipped between the two originally dispatched hazmat buckets; 11_hazmat_b covering 9.5.3 onward: driving/parking rules, emergencies, required notification, and the glossary); Section 10 School Bus mapped to 12_school_bus; Section 11 Vehicle Inspection (modernized, revised March 2025) mapped to 13_vehicle_inspection; Section 12 Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test and Section 13 On-Road Driving combined into 14_basic_control_onroad. Some sections (Transporting Cargo Safely, Doubles and Triples, Tank Vehicles) are naturally short in this manual and their question buckets were sized down accordingly rather than padded to match larger sections. Every question in this bank is grounded in a specific passage of the fetched official New Jersey manual text (or, for exam-mechanics-adjacent process facts, the official nj.gov/mvc/drivertopics/cdltest.htm page) cited in that question's source_note; none are invented, generic, or borrowed from another state's numbers.
